assumptions.condition: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed with law \(P^{\mathrm{obs}}\).
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(m_{t,P}\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on the closed \(h_0\)-neighborhood of \(B\) within \(D\).

standard.name: Lipschitz continuity at an RD boundary

assumptions.condition: For every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), \(E_P[\exp\{\lambda[Y-Tm_{1,P}(X)-(1-T)m_{0,P}(X)]\}\mid X,T]\leq\exp(\sigma^2\lambda^2/2)\) almost surely.
\(q_t(x,h)\geq c_mh^\kappa\) for every \(x\in B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\leq h_0\).

novel.justification: Polynomial one-sided depletion occurs when a bivariate score density behaves as \(|r|^{\kappa-2}\) transverse to an eligibility boundary; the normalized flat densities give concrete examples.
A threshold-thin site models a localized geographic or administrative support bottleneck.
A normalized radial-power density realizes the envelope because sites below a mass threshold occupy a centered interval.
A density proportional to \(|r|^{\kappa-2}\) realizes transverse scarcity along the entire flat boundary.

definitions.name: One-sided ball masses
definitions.construction: For \(x\in B\) and \(0<h\leq h_0\), set \(q_t(x,h)=P\{X\in A_t,\|X-x\|_2\leq h\}\) and \(a_P(x,h)=\min\{q_0(x,h),q_1(x,h)\}\).

definitions.name: Thin-site packing profile
definitions.construction: \(J_P(h,u)=\max\{|F|:F\subseteq\{x\in B:a_P(x,h)\leq u\},\|x-x'\|_2\geq h\text{ for distinct }x,x'\in F\}\), with value zero for an empty thin set.

definitions.name: Base polynomial-thickness causal class
definitions.construction: \(\mathrm{Base}_\kappa=\{P:P\text{ satisfies }\mathsf A_{\mathrm{sharp}},\mathsf A_{\mathrm{cons}},\mathsf A_{\mathrm{Lip}},\mathsf A_{\mathrm{env}},\mathsf A_{\mathrm{subG}},\mathsf A_{\mathrm{mass}}\text{ at }\kappa\}\).

definitions.name: Isolated-thinning class
definitions.construction: \(\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa=\{P\in\mathrm{Base}_\kappa:P\text{ satisfies }\mathsf A_{\mathrm{one}}\text{ and }\mathsf A_{\mathrm{iso}}\text{ for every displayed }h,u\}\).

definitions.name: Causal Gaussian tent experiments
definitions.construction: For \(0<h\leq\min\{h_0,1/3\}\), choose \(3h\)-separated \(x_j\in B\), set \(\psi_{j,h}(z)=(1-\|z-x_j\|_2/h)_+\) and \(a_{\mathrm{tent}}=Lh/4\). Let \(Z_0,Z_1\) be independent standard Gaussians independent of \(X\), set \(T=\mathbf1\{R\geq0\}\) and \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\). The baseline laws use the corresponding flat density and \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\); each tent law instead uses \(Y(1)=a_{\mathrm{tent}}\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_1\) and \(Y(0)=-a_{\mathrm{tent}}\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_0\).

definitions.name: Total split-sample empirical-packing estimator
definitions.construction: Split the sample into \(I_1\) and \(I_2\). Let \(H_n=\{h_02^{-j}:0\leq j\leq\lceil\log_2n\rceil\}\) and \(U_n=\{0,1\}\cup\{2^{-\ell}:0\leq\ell\leq\lceil\log_2(n_1\vee1)\rceil\}\). On \(I_1\), set \(\widehat q^{(1)}_t(x,h)=(n_1\vee1)^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_1}\mathbf1\{X_i\in A_t,\|X_i-x\|_2\leq h\}\). With \(b_n(v)=\sqrt{12v\log(en)/(n_1\vee1)}+20\log(en)/(n_1\vee1)\), set \(q^U_t=\min\{1,\widehat q^{(1)}_t+b_n(\widehat q^{(1)}_t)\}\), \(q^L_t=\max\{0,\widehat q^{(1)}_t-b_n(\widehat q^{(1)}_t)\}\), \(a^U=\min_tq^U_t\), and \(a^L=\min_tq^L_t\). For each \(h\in H_n\), form the finite source-labeled list consisting of \((-1/2,0,0)\), \((1/2,0,1)\), and every \((S_i+e\sqrt{h^2-R_i^2},i,e)\) with \(i\in I_1\), \(e\in\{-1,1\}\), \(|R_i|\leq h\), and \(S_i+e\sqrt{h^2-R_i^2}\in[-1/2,1/2]\). Sort lexicographically by boundary coordinate, then by \(i\), then by \(e\), and discard repeated coordinates after retaining the least source label. Write the remaining coordinates as \(-1/2=z_0<\cdots<z_M=1/2\), define \(C_1(h)=((0,z_0),\ldots,(0,z_M))\), and set \(G_1(h)=\{(0,z_j):0\leq j\leq M\}\cup\{(0,(z_j+z_{j+1})/2):0\leq j<M\}\). For \(v\in[0,1]\), round \(v\) upward to the smallest \(u(v)\in U_n\) and set \(\widehat J(h,v)=1\vee\max\{|F|:F\subseteq G_1(h),\|x-x'\|_2\geq h/2,a^U(x,h/4)\leq u(v)\}\). Let \(\widehat u(x,h)\) be the smallest severity layer at least \(\min\{1,4a^U(x,h)\}\). On \(I_2\), set \(N^{(2)}_t(x,h)=\sum_{i\in I_2}\mathbf1\{X_i\in A_t,\|X_i-x\|_2\leq h\}\) and define the raw average everywhere by \(\widetilde Y^{(2)}_t(x,h)=0\) when \(N^{(2)}_t(x,h)=0\), and \(\widetilde Y^{(2)}_t(x,h)=N^{(2)}_t(x,h)^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_2}Y_i\mathbf1\{X_i\in A_t,\|X_i-x\|_2\leq h\}\) otherwise. Set \(\overline Y^{(2)}_t(x,h)=\Pi_L(\widetilde Y^{(2)}_t(x,h))\). Among \(h\in H_n\) with \(n_2a^L(x,h)\geq64\{1+\log(e\widehat J(h,\widehat u(x,h)))\}\), choose the smallest minimizer of \(Lh+4\sigma\sqrt{\{1+\log(e\widehat J(h,\widehat u(x,h)))\}/\{n_2a^L(x,h)\}}\); set \(\widehat h(x)=h_0\) when this set is empty. Finally set \(\widehat\tau_n(x)=\Pi_{2L}(\overline Y^{(2)}_1(x,\widehat h(x))-\overline Y^{(2)}_0(x,\widehat h(x)))\).

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathrm{Base}_\kappa\), sharp assignment and consistency give \(g_{t,P}=m_{t,P}\) on the restricted support in \(A_t\). The mass condition places every \(x\in B\) in the closure of both supports, so the Lipschitz representatives have unique side limits. Hence \(\theta_{t,P}(x)=\lim_{z\to x,z\in A_t}E_{P^{\mathrm{obs}}}[Y\mid X=z,T=t]\), and \(\tau_P(x)=m_{1,P}(x)-m_{0,P}(x)\) is identified on \(B\).
statements.justification: The statistical target is an observed-law functional with a causal interpretation.
statements.gap: Published boundary-curve identification is stated under positive density; this lemma allows polynomially vanishing side mass.
statements.consumer: Boundary-discontinuity analysts can interpret oracle risk as error for the boundary average treatment-effect curve.

statements.statement: For every \(\kappa\in K\), the Cartesian formulas define Borel score laws with support \(D\). With \(c_m=2^{-(\bar\kappa-2)-5}\), \(C_m=2^{\bar\kappa-2}+1\), \(c_J=1\), and \(C_{\mathrm{iso}}=5+4\cdot8^{1/\epsilon}\), \(P^{0,\mathrm{iso}}\in\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa\) and \(P^{0,\mathrm{perv}}\in\mathrm{Perv}_\kappa\). For every \(x=(0,s_0)\in B\) and \(0<h\leq h_0\), \(2^{-\alpha-3}h^\kappa\leq q_t^{\mathrm{perv}}(x,h)\leq h^\kappa/2\), \(q_t^{\mathrm{iso}}(x,h)\geq2^{-\alpha-5}h^\kappa\), and \(q_t^{\mathrm{iso}}(x,h)\leq2^\alpha h^2(|s_0|+h)^\alpha\); when \(|s_0|\geq2h\), also \(q_t^{\mathrm{iso}}(x,h)\geq2^{-\alpha-3}h^2|s_0|^\alpha\). At the origin, \(q_t^{\mathrm{iso}}(0,h)=D_\alpha h^\kappa\), and the isolated packing envelope holds for every admissible \(u\), including \(u=1\). Every tent law is a Borel causal law in the same profile class, obeys consistency, has \(L\)-Lipschitz means, and separates \(\tau_P\) from the baseline by \(Lh/2\) at its active center. The squared-tent identities are \(\int_D\psi_{j,h}^2f_{\mathrm{perv},\alpha}=Q_{\mathrm{perv},\alpha}h^\kappa\) and \(\int_D\psi_{0,h}^2f_{\mathrm{iso},\alpha}=Q_{\mathrm{iso},\alpha}h^\kappa\). Hence \(\mathrm{KL}((P^{j,h,\mathrm{perv}}_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},(P^{0,\mathrm{perv}}_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n})=nL^2Q_{\mathrm{perv},\alpha}h^{\kappa+2}/(32\sigma^2)\), with the isolated coefficients at the centered site. Constants are uniform over \(K\). At \(\kappa=3\), \(Q_{\mathrm{perv},1}=1/15\) and the divergence is \(nL^2h^5/(480\sigma^2)\).
statements.justification: This attributed supporting result records the normalized witness and divergence calculation from the banked \(\texttt{stat\_bdd\_thickness\_estimability\_frontier}\) analysis.
statements.gap: No separate novelty is claimed for the witness; it certifies that the endpoint classes used by the oracle theorem are nonempty causal-law classes.
statements.consumer: It supplies auditable class-membership and information checks for the estimator theorem.

statements.statement: There are constants \(c,C\) and events \(\mathcal E_n\) with \(\inf_{P\in\bigcup_{\kappa\in K}\mathrm{Base}_\kappa}P(\mathcal E_n)\geq1-Cn^{-3}\) such that, simultaneously for \(h\in H_n\) and \(u\in U_n\) satisfying \(n_1u\geq C\log(en)\), \[J_P(h,u)\leq\widehat J(h,c\{u+\log(en)/n_1\})\leq C J_P(h/8,C\{u+\log(en)/n_1\}).\] On \(\mathcal E_n\), \(a^L(x,h)\leq a_P(x,h)\leq a^U(x,h)\) for every \(x,h\), and the bounds are within constant factors when \(n_1a_P(x,h)\geq C\log(en)\). For every \(h\in H_n\), the source-labeled lexicographic sorting, duplicate removal, and midpoint map defining \(C_1(h)\) and \(G_1(h)\) are Borel functions of \((X_i)_{i\in I_1}\); the finite maximum defining \(\widehat J(h,u)\) is therefore Borel for every \(u\in U_n\). The confidence calibration, zero-count event, and \(h_0\)-fallback event together contribute at most \(C(L+\sigma)\log^2(en)/n\) to expected supremum risk and introduce no leading global \(\log n\) factor on \(\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa\).
statements.justification: This proof-critical component prevents both an implicit selector and a hidden global logarithm in Theorem 1.
statements.gap: Design-adaptive regression does not supply the measurable severity-layer packing comparison needed for this boundary oracle theorem; the lemma is supporting rather than a second headline claim.
statements.consumer: It certifies that the implementable penalty distinguishes localized support holes from pervasive scarcity without measurability gaps.

statements.statement: The total estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\) is Borel measurable, is defined on zero-count samples and empty admissible-bandwidth sets, and uses neither \(\kappa\) nor the profile class. There is a finite constant \(C\), uniform over \(K\), such that for every \(\kappa\in K\) and \(P\in\mathrm{Base}_\kappa\), \[E_P\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty\leq C\sup_{x\in B}\inf_{h\in H_n}\left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{1+\log\bigl(eJ_P(h,\min\{1,Ca_P(x,h)\})\bigr)}{n a_P(x,h)}}\right\}+C\sigma\frac{\log^2(en)}n+4L\,P\left\{\exists x\in B:\min_{t\in\{0,1\}}N^{(2)}_t(x,\widehat h(x))=0\ \mathbin{\text{or}}\ \nexists h\in H_n,\ n_2a^L(x,h)\geq64\bigl[1+\log\{e\widehat J(h,\widehat u(x,h))\}\bigr]\right\}.\] Moreover the displayed event probability is at most \(C\log^2(en)/n\), so the last two terms are bounded by \(C(L+\sigma)\log^2(en)/n\).
statements.justification: The packing-oracle inequality is the sole closed novelty claim and makes local thin-site multiplicity, rather than global boundary cardinality, determine the stochastic penalty.
statements.gap: Gaiffas (2007) gives pointwise adaptation and Gaiffas (2009) gives spatial normalization for finitely many zeros; neither gives this measurable unweighted boundary-supremum profile oracle.
statements.consumer: Practitioners obtain a fully defined density-free causal-curve estimator without knowing the depletion exponent or regime.

statements.statement: Corollary (same-estimator consequence for the endpoint classes of \(\texttt{stat\_bdd\_thickness\_estimability\_frontier}\)). There is a finite constant \(C\), uniform over \(K\), such that for every \(\kappa\in K\) and all sufficiently large \(n\), the single total estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\), without knowledge of \(\kappa\) or the endpoint class, satisfies \[\sup_{P\in\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa}E_P\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty\leq Cn^{-1/(\kappa+2)},\qquad \sup_{P\in\mathrm{Perv}_\kappa}E_P\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty\leq C(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.\]
statements.justification: The endpoint minimax orders are established in the banked \(\texttt{stat\_bdd\_thickness\_estimability\_frontier}\) result; this corollary records only the new simultaneous attainment consequence of Theorem 1.
statements.gap: The banked result supplies separate endpoint procedures and minimax benchmarks, but not one total \(\kappa\)-free and profile-free estimator attaining both endpoint upper rates.
statements.consumer: Analysts can use one causal boundary-curve procedure without selecting an isolated or pervasive support regime.

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from a causal law with sharp flat-boundary assignment; only the observed law is available.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment overlap holds at a fixed score; smooth potential-outcome means and positive one-sided support identify both traces.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: First-half scores determine a fully explicit finite grid and estimate masses and packing counts; total clipped second-half side averages estimate the traces. Neither \(\kappa\), the density, nor the profile class is estimated parametrically.

estimand_functional: \(\tau_P(x)=\lim_{z\to x,z\in A_1}E_{P^{\mathrm{obs}}}[Y\mid X=z,T=1]-\lim_{z\to x,z\in A_0}E_{P^{\mathrm{obs}}}[Y\mid X=z,T=0]\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives the pointwise minimax order \(n^{-s/(1+2s+\beta)}\) up to a slowly varying factor under regular variation.
The paper constructs an adaptive estimator attaining the pointwise rate at a degenerate-design target under inhomogeneous design.
The upper and localized lower results establish spatially varying sup-norm normalization with finitely many polynomial density zeros.
The exact minimax sup-norm constant is derived when the design density has a positive minimum.
The submanifold-integral result derives its minimax rate under a design density bounded above and away from zero near the target submanifold.
The sharp boundary-effect-curve result gives pointwise and uniform location-based rates on a continuous score-density class bounded away from zero near the boundary.
Theorem 6 gives an isotropic boundary minimax result on a continuous score-density class bounded above and away from zero near the boundary.

tldr: A single total measurable split-sample estimator adapts to the unknown multiplicity of polynomially thin sites along an identified causal boundary trace. A deterministic source-labeled ordering produces the first-half grid and upper-confidence packing counts, while zero-defined and envelope-clipped second-half side averages produce the trace estimate. The population packing-oracle inequality is the sole closed novelty claim. Its explicit remainder covers zero counts and the \(h_0\)-fallback event and yields, for the same estimator, the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) and pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\); the endpoint minimax benchmarks and normalized witnesses are attributed to the banked parent result.

project_justification.gap: Degenerate-design theory treats one point or finitely many one-dimensional zeros, while boundary-curve theory assumes density bounded away from zero. Neither gives a total unweighted-supremum estimator that measurably learns thin-site multiplicity.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a profile-adaptive estimator whose stochastic penalty is the packing entropy at each site's local mass severity, with all sample-dependent selections defined on every realization.
project_justification.fill: The project constructs an explicit ordered first-half grid, estimates its packing entropy, uses zero-defined clipped second-half side averages, proves a population oracle inequality with an event-explicit negligible remainder, and derives both endpoint rates from one procedure.

related_work: Gaiffas (2005) supplies the single-site bias--information equation. Gaiffas (2007), "On pointwise adaptive curve estimation based on inhomogeneous data," ESAIM: Probability and Statistics 11, pages 344--364, studies pointwise adaptation at a degenerate-design target. The distinct Statistica Sinica paper of Gaiffas (2009), volume 19, pages 427--447, establishes uniform estimation with spatial normalization for finitely many one-dimensional density zeros. Neither paper estimates boundary packing multiplicity under one unweighted supremum loss. Antoniadis, Pensky, and Sapatinas (2014) study global adaptation for inhomogeneous one-dimensional designs. Bertin (2004) gives the positive-density supremum benchmark. Xiaohong Chen and Wayne Yuan Gao (2026), Cowles Foundation Discussion Paper 2450R1 (March 2026), derive a submanifold-integral minimax rate under positive bounded design density; that scalar positive-density rate informs the geometric comparison but does not address a boundary trace with polynomial side-mass depletion. Hahn, Todd, and van der Klaauw (2001) supply the causal identification logic. Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu formulate location-based and distance-based boundary results on a continuous-score-density class bounded away from zero near the boundary. The first nontrivial result here is instead the profile-packing oracle inequality and its same-estimator isolated/pervasive upper-rate adaptation under polynomial two-sided depletion. The banked \(\texttt{stat\_bdd\_uniform\_log\_penalty}\) result proves a positive-density distance-rule converse. It varies an estimator-information restriction while maintaining regular local mass, so it neither supplies nor rules out a frontier driven by the multiplicity of polynomially thin sites.
technical_internal_limitation: Scalar side mass does not imply coercivity of higher-order local-polynomial Gram matrices, so the estimator uses local averages. It treats \(L\) and \(\sigma\) as fixed known class constants. Constants are uniform only on compact exponent sets bounded away from \(2\).
honest_scope: The profile-adaptive packing-oracle inequality is the sole closed novelty claim. Identification, the measurable empirical-packing comparison, and flat-law validity support that theorem. The estimator is total: empty side counts map to zero before clipping, an empty admissible set maps to \(h_0\), and the final contrast is clipped to \([-2L,2L]\). The endpoint minimax orders belong to the banked \(\texttt{stat\_bdd\_thickness\_estimability\_frontier}\) result; the corollary here claims only simultaneous upper-rate attainment by one estimator. At \(\kappa=3\), the retained witness divergence is \(nL^2h^5/(480\sigma^2)\). Formally setting \(\kappa=2\) in the balances recovers the bivariate Lipschitz pointwise rate \(n^{-1/4}\) and uniform rate \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\), without uniform constants at that excluded endpoint.

novelty_justification: Gaiffas (2007) adapts at one degenerate-design point, whereas the distinct Gaiffas (2009) uniform paper uses location-specific normalization for finitely many one-dimensional zeros. Boundary-discontinuity theory studies a causal curve on a continuous-score-density class bounded away from zero. The first nontrivial result here, and the sole closed novelty claim, is the packing-oracle inequality for one total measurable estimator whose empirical penalty learns the number of comparably thin boundary sites. Its attributed endpoint corollary records same-estimator isolated/pervasive upper-rate adaptation under polynomial two-sided depletion without re-claiming the banked minimax lower bounds. The explicit finite selector and event-explicit remainder close the measurability gap without changing the field-tier kernel, while the packing-comparison lemma ensures uniform calibration does not reinstate the global logarithm removed in the isolated regime.
